He played one year of [[college basketball]] with the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] before he was drafted in the [[2010 NBA draft]] by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. He played four and a half seasons in the NBA between 2010 and 2014. He finished his career in 2017 after two seasons in the [[NBA G League]]. ==Early life== Henry was born in [[Ghent]], [[Belgium]], where his father played professional basketball in the early 1990s.Jenni Carlson. "[http://newsok.com/article/3212515/1204780472 Xavier Henry has plenty of reasons to keep smiling]". NewsOK.com. March 6, 2008. Retrieved on April 4, 2009. ==High school career== Henry attended [[Putnam City High School]] in [[Oklahoma City|Oklahoma City, Oklahoma]]. He missed the start of his of senior season after he fractured his [[Zygomatic bone|cheekbone]] in a [[Traffic collision|car accident]] in October 2008.{{cite web|title=Xavier Henry to decide in the Spring |url=http://theshiver.com/2008/11/xavier-henry-to-decide-in-the-spring/ |work=TheShiver.com |date=November 6, 2008 |access-date=November 6, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121113153422/http://theshiver.com/2008/11/xavier-henry-to-decide-in-the-spring/ |archive-date=November 13, 2012 }} On March 14, 2009, he led Putnam City to the Oklahoma Class 6A state championship, scoring 24 points in the title game against Jenks High School.Ryan Aber. "[http://newsok.com/class-6a-boys-putnam-city-routs-jenks-for-trophy/article/3353606 Class 6A boys: Putnam City routs Jenks for trophy]". NewsOK.com. March 15, 2009. Retrieved on March 21, 2009. Henry was named to the [[2009 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2009 McDonald's All-American Game]] where he scored 14 points.{{cite web|title=Wednesday's McDonald's All-American Game box scores|url=http://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/wednesdays-mcdonalds-all-american-game-box-scores/?|work=SeattleTimes.com|date=April 2, 2009|access-date=April 2, 2009}} Henry was also selected to play in the 2009 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] at the [[Moda Center|Rose Garden]] in [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]] where he led Team USA with 22 points including six [[Three-point field goal|3-pointers]]{{cite web|title=World stars surprise USA at Nike Hoop Summit|url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=934728|work=Rivals.com|date=April 12, 2009|access-date=April 12, 2009|archive-date=April 12, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090412223127/http://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=934728|url-status=dead}} and the Jordan Brand Classic at [[Madison Square Garden]] where he scored 10 points for the white team.{{cite web|title=Big men shine in Jordan Brand Classic|url=https://www.espn.com/highschool/rise/basketball/boys/news/story?id=4080678|work=ESPN.com|date=April 19, 2009|access-date=April 19, 2009}} He was [[Slam (magazine)|''SLAM'']] magazine's high school diary keeper for the 2008–09 basketball season.Ryan Jones. "[http://slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2009/03/xavier-henry-will-be-televised/ Xavier Henry Will Be Televised] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090321014209/http://slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2009/03/xavier-henry-will-be-televised/ |date=March 21, 2009 }}". ''SLAM Online''. March 19, 2009. Retrieved on March 21, 2009. ===Recruitment=== By the end of his senior season, Henry was ranked as the #6 overall prospect and #2 [[shooting guard]] in the class of 2009 by [[Scout.com]],{{cite web|title=Scout Top 100 |url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=88&yr=2009 |work=Scout.com |access-date=November 18, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131212084730/http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=88&yr=2009 |archive-date=December 12, 2013 }} #8 overall and #3 shooting guard by [[Rivals.com]]{{cite web|title=Rivals Top 150|url=https://rivals.yahoo.com/kansas/football/recruiting/rankings/rank-1642/0|work=Rivals.com|access-date=November 18, 2008}} and #3 overall, #2 shooting guard by [[ESPN]].{{cite web|title=ESPNU 100 |url=http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/espnu100?&season=2009&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fespnu100%3f%26season%3d2009 |work=ESPN.com |access-date=November 18, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090209130701/http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/espnu100?&season=2009&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fespnu100%3f%26season%3d2009 |archive-date=February 9, 2009 }} Originally, Henry was heavily recruited by both [[University of Memphis|Memphis]] and [[University of Kansas|Kansas]]. On November 18, 2008, Henry announced his commitment to Memphis citing the opportunity to play alongside his brother, C. J., as the primary reason for the decision.{{cite web|title=Henry picks Memphis|url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2008/nov/18/henry-picks-memphis/|work=KUSports.com|date=November 18, 2008|access-date=November 18, 2008}} In March 2009, Memphis's head coach [[John Calipari]] took the head coaching job at the [[University of Kentucky]], prompting Henry to reopen his recruitment.{{Cite web|last=Pennington|first=James|title=Father of No. 1 recruit, Xavier Henry, says he will decommit from Memphis|url=http://kykernel.com/2009/03/31/father-of-no-1-recruit-xavier-henry-says-he-will-decommit-from-memphis/|website=[[The Kentucky Kernel]]|date=March 31, 2009|access-date=October 16, 2022|archive-date=July 10, 2012|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120710163551/http://kykernel.com/2009/03/31/father-of-no-1-recruit-xavier-henry-says-he-will-decommit-from-memphis/|url-status=dead}} On April 23, Henry officially announced his choice to play basketball for Kansas.{{cite web|title=Xavier Henry announces he's coming to KU|url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2009/apr/23/xavier-henry-announces-hes-coming-ku/|work=KUSports.com|date=April 23, 2009|access-date=April 23, 2009}} {{cquote|I grew up always wanting to go to Kansas. I switched to Memphis because my brother was going there. Now, with coach (John Calipari) leaving (for Kentucky), we've decided to go to KU. I'm really excited. That's where my whole family played.|||Xavier Henry}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2009}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Xavier Henry | position = SG | hometown = Oklahoma City | highschool = [[Putnam City High School|Putnam City]] | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 210 | 40 = | commitdate = April 23, 2009 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | espn grade = 98 }} |- |} ==College career== [[File:20091219 Manny Harris guarded by Xavier Henry.jpg|thumb|Henry guarding future [[Los Angeles Lakers|Lakers]] and [[Los Angeles D-Fenders|D-Fenders]] teammate [[Manny Harris]] of [[2009–10 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] on December 19, 2009]] Henry scored 27 points in his first college game, breaking the record for most points scored by a Jayhawk in a debut game as a freshman.J. Brady McCollough. "[http://www.kansascity.com/sports/story/1569458.html Henry sets KU debut record for freshman with 27 points]". ''Kansas City Star''. November 13, 2009. Retrieved on November 14, 2009. On December 12, 2009, Henry scored 31 points against [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle]] at the [[Sprint Center]] in [[Kansas City, Kansas|Kansas City]]. In doing so he became the first KU freshman to score 30 points in a game since [[Paul Pierce]]. Henry's 31 points was four short of the KU record for points scored by a freshman set by KU legend [[Danny Manning]].{{Cite web|last=Bedore|first=Gary|date=2009-12-13|title=Most excellent: Henry scores 31 in rout of Explorers|url=https://www2.kusports.com/news/2009/dec/13/most-excellent/|access-date=2022-10-16|website=KUsports.com|language=en}} ===College statistics=== {{NBA player statistics acquired by [[New Orleans Pelicans|New Orleans Hornets]] as a part of a three-team trade that sent [[Marreese Speights]] to [[Memphis Grizzlies|Memphis]] and two future second-round picks to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|title=HORNETS ACQUIRE HENRY|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_acquire_henry_2012_01_04.html|work=NBA.com|date=January 4, 2012|access-date=January 4, 2012}} Henry was assigned to the [[Iowa Wolves|Iowa Energy]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]] on March 17, 2012{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/hornets_assign_henry_2012_03_18.html|title=New Orleans Hornets Assign Xavier Henry to Iowa Energy|work=NBA.com|date=March 17, 2012|access-date=March 17, 2012}} and recalled on March 19.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/hornets_recall_xavier_henry_2012_03_19.html|title=HORNETS RECALL XAVIER HENRY FROM IOWA ENERGY|work=NBA.com|date=March 19, 2012|access-date=March 19, 2012}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2013–2014)=== On September 5, 2013, Henry signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/130905xavierhenry|title=Lakers Sign Xavier Henry|work=NBA.com|date=September 5, 2013|access-date=September 5, 2013}} In his debut on October 29, 2013, he led the Lakers to a 116–103 victory over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] while scoring a career-high 22 points.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131029/LACLAL/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Lakers 116, Clippers 103|work=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2013|access-date=October 29, 2013}} On February 27, 2014, he was assigned to the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140227_henry|title=Xavier Henry Assigned to the D-Fenders|work=NBA.com|date=February 27, 2014|access-date=February 27, 2014}} On March 2, 2014, he was recalled by the Lakers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140302xavierhenry_recalled|title=Lakers Recall Xavier Henry|work=NBA.com|date=March 2, 2014|access-date=March 2, 2014}} On April 11, 2014, Henry underwent surgery to repair both a torn ligament in his left wrist and a cartilage abnormality in his right knee.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140411xavierhenry_surgeries|title=Xavier Henry Undergoes Successful Surgeries|work=NBA.com|date=April 11, 2014|access-date=April 11, 2014}} On July 25, 2014, Henry re-signed with the Lakers{{cite web|title=Lakers Re-sign Xavier Henry|date=July 25, 2014|work=NBA.com|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140725_henry_resign|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140811025439/http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140725_henry_resign/?cid=TW|archive-date=August Henry Agrees Upon One-Year, $1M Deal With Lakers|work=RealGM.com|date=July 18, 2014|access-date=July 18, 2014}} On October 18, 2014, Henry's agents announced that he would be seeking a second opinion 2014, he was reassigned to the Los Angeles D-Fenders.{{cite web | url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=16829 | title=Lakers assign Jordan Clarkson and Xavier Henry to D-League | work=InsideHoops.com | date=November 15, 2014 | access-date=November 15, 2014}} He was recalled the next day. On November 22, he was reassigned to D-Fenders{{cite web | url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=16867 | title=Lakers re-assign Jordan Clarkson and Xavier Henry to D-League | work=InsideHoops.com | date=November 22, 2014 | access-date=November 22, 2014}} and again recalled a day later.
